partners.mechanism_chain: NT5E (HGNC:8007) —DISRUPTS→ ATP hydrolysis to AMP and pyrophosphate (GO:0008885); ATP hydrolysis to AMP and pyrophosphate (GO:0008885) —DECREASES→ Pyrophosphate (PPi) (CHEBI:38676); Pyrophosphate (PPi) (CHEBI:38676) —DECREASES→ Inhibition of vascular smooth muscle cell calcification (GO:0045745); Inhibition of vascular smooth muscle cell calcification (GO:0045745) —LEADS_TO→ Arterial calcification (HP:0001695); NADSYN1 (HGNC:24141) —DISRUPTS→ NAD+ biosynthesis (GO:0006702); NAD+ biosynthesis (GO:0006702) —DECREASES→ NAD+ (CHEBI:17995); NAD+ (CHEBI:17995) —DECREASES→ Regulation of extracellular matrix organization (GO:0061005); Regulation of extracellular matrix organization (GO:0061005) —LEADS_TO→ Vertebral defects (HP:0000961); Regulation of extracellular matrix organization (GO:0061005) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiac defects (HP:0001627); Regulation of extracellular matrix organization (GO:0061005) —LEADS_TO→ Renal defects (HP:0000076); Regulation of extracellular matrix organization (GO:0061005) —LEADS_TO→ Limb defects (HP:0001159). Loss-of-function mutations in NT5E lead to reduced hydrolysis of ATP to AMP and pyrophosphate (PPi), resulting in decreased PPi levels. PPi is a known inhibitor of vascular calcification. Reduced PPi thus promotes arterial calcification, a hallmark of HAAS. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in NADSYN1 impair NAD+ biosynthesis, leading to reduced NAD+ levels. NAD+ is crucial for various cellular processes, including those regulated by sirtuins, which are involved in extracellular matrix organization and integrity. Dysregulation of extracellular matrix organization contributes to the diverse developmental defects seen in VCRLR3, including vertebral, cardiac, renal, and limb abnormalities. The shared convergence is on the regulation of extracellular matrix integrity, albeit through different molecular mediators (PPi vs. NAD+ dependent pathways).

partners.mechanism_chain: NT5E (HGNC:17869) —DISRUPTS→ Purine salvage pathway / Nucleotide metabolism (GO:0006284); Purine salvage pathway / Nucleotide metabolism (GO:0006284) —DECREASES→ Adenosine (CHEBI:15870); Adenosine (CHEBI:15870) —DECREASES→ Extracellular Matrix Organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular Matrix Organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Arterial calcification (HP:0002670); DPYS (HGNC:2883) —DISRUPTS→ Dihydropyrimidine (CHEBI:17649); Dihydropyrimidine (CHEBI:17649) —INCREASES→ Purine salvage pathway / Nucleotide metabolism (GO:0006284); Purine salvage pathway / Nucleotide metabolism (GO:0006284) —LEADS_TO→ Dihydropyrimidinuria (HP:0030741). Loss-of-function mutations in NT5E disrupt purine salvage and nucleotide metabolism, leading to decreased adenosine, which in turn impairs extracellular matrix organization and results in arterial calcification. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in DPYS disrupt dihydropyrimidine metabolism, causing accumulation of dihydropyrimidines, which further perturb nucleotide metabolism and contribute to dihydropyrimidinuria. The convergence occurs at the level of nucleotide metabolism, affecting downstream processes that impact extracellular matrix and cellular function, ultimately manifesting in the distinct yet mechanistically related phenotypes.

partners.mechanism_chain: NT5E (HGNC:8003) —DISRUPTS→ ENPP1 activity (GO:0004120); ENPP1 activity (GO:0004120) —DECREASES→ Extracellular pyrophosphate (PPi) (CHEBI:17606); Extracellular pyrophosphate (PPi) (CHEBI:17606) —LEADS_TO→ Ectopic calcification (HP:0002713); DPYD (HGNC:2960) —DISRUPTS→ Pyrimidine catabolism (R-HSA-1937095); Pyrimidine catabolism (R-HSA-1937095) —DECREASES→ Uracil (CHEBI:17907); Uracil (CHEBI:17907) —INCREASES→ Nucleotide salvage pathway (R-HSA-57024); Nucleotide salvage pathway (R-HSA-57024) —LEADS_TO→ Neurological abnormalities (HP:0000750).
